subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron/proactive message delivery with no explicit `delivery.accountId`, should the resolver prefer the agent/channel binding over session `lastAccountId`, keep the current session-first behavior, or fail closed when both are plausible?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but changing this precedence is a compatibility- and security-sensitive behavior choice for existing multi-account cron setups.

options.title: Prefer binding before session account
options.body: Keep explicit job `accountId` first, then use the unique agent/channel binding, and only use session account when it cannot conflict with that binding.

options.title: Fail closed on ambiguity
options.body: When a session account and bound account differ, refuse delivery and ask the operator to set `delivery.accountId` explicitly.

options.title: Keep session-first behavior
options.body: Preserve compatibility but document that cron jobs must set `accountId` explicitly to avoid wrong-account delivery.

recommendation.title: Prefer binding before session account
recommendation.body: Keep explicit job `accountId` first, then use the unique agent/channel binding, and only use session account when it cannot conflict with that binding.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete committed the binding-fallback change and is a strong routing candidate for a security-sensitive precedence decision.
